identity.name: mission
identity.purpose: Mission Control is a **local-first control centre** for a personal ecosystem of applied-AI projects, books, research programmes and commercial work. Its declared purpose is coordination, not replacement: it answers what matters today, where work stopped, which evidence already exists, what can be launched safely, and what should happen next (`README.md`, `pyproject.toml` description "Local-first control centre for an ecosystem of applied-AI projects").

gaps: No live execution was authorized: no endpoint was called, no browser session was run, no managed process was launched, no Docker container was started, no migration was applied and no model/CLI call was made. Every operational_status is therefore bounded at tested-not-demonstrated or source-inspected-only.
The packaged SPA behaviour was inferred from frontend/src and frontend tests only; frontend/dist was not built or served during this inspection.

Frontend page/component inventory was sampled (HomePage, InboxPage, CommandPalette and the Living Book/Experiments surfaces) rather than exhaustively enumerated; capabilities.json cites frontend files as evidence for backend capabilities instead of describing every page separately.

Platform settings, Platform security and Platform persistence are each represented by a single capability; their internal helpers (retention policy, log rotation, background monitor loop, logging configuration) were not separately inventoried.

External engine internals (Next schema, Work CLI contract, CoCoder report schema, Writer summary schema, ALIVE endpoints, Worker API) were taken from Mission Control's client/adapter code and documentation; the external systems themselves are outside this repository and were not inspected.
The cultivation GitHub path depends on gh/REST credentials that were not present for inspection; only the code path and its tests were reviewed.

scripts/*.py helper scripts (capture_repo_states.py, demo_live_review.py, prove_restart.py, smoke_git_activity.py, workbench_browser_test.py, gen_prompt_example.py) are operational helpers and were not promoted to capabilities.
Test-level evidence cites test source files; the pytest suite was not executed, so no test result is asserted.
